title: Before Chandrayaan, Mangalyaan, there was Nike-Apache: India's 1st sounding rocket launch
content: On November 21, 1963, India launched its first sounding rocket from Thumba, establishing its space program. The rocket, Nike-Apache, carried instruments for atmospheric studies and marked a major milestone. Established by Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, the Indian National Committee for Space Research organized early research and development. Following this, the Indian Space Research Organisation was formed in 1969 and developed indigenous rockets.

title: In 1913, Ohio parents mailed their 10-pound baby to grandmother for 15 cents

title: Bat Species Survey: Madidi records 99 bat species; seven are new national records
content: In a groundbreaking study, scientists have discovered 99 bat species in Bolivia's Madidi National Park, marking the first sightings of seven species in the nation. Employing diverse methods for capturing and monitoring these fascinating creatures across various altitudes, the research highlights the park's critical role in preserving bat habitats and its exceptional biodiversity, underscoring the urgent need to protect this vital ecosystem for the health of these species.

title: MacKenzie Scott gives $2M each to 279 nonprofits from $640M fund

The selected organizations focused on issues related to economic disparities, education, healthcare, and discrimination. Scott's approach shifted from private research to an open call, increasing both funding and recipients. This effort follows her significant charitable donations made after her divorce from Jeff Bezos.

title: As Florida uses robot rabbits to catch pythons; study reveals when snakes climb trees
content: In 2025, Florida implemented solar-powered robotic rabbit decoys designed to attract Burmese pythons for removal efforts. Researchers tracked 346 pythons from 2017 to 2024 to study their climbing behavior. The study found that juvenile pythons are more likely to climb trees compared to adults. A recent competition in 2026 resulted in 280 pythons being removed by participants. Since 2017, over 19,000 pythons have been captured in Florida through organized efforts.
